SUNDELLO / WORKFORCE HOUSING

Rooms near the work.

Outpost puts private rooms with their own bath close to the job, on ground screws, from a single unit to a camp. Here is how it fits six kinds of work.

Find your marketMeet Outpost

WHO IT IS FOR

One unit family.
Six kinds of work.

The same Outpost units, fitted to each job: where they go, who lives in them, how they are paid for and what happens when the work moves on.

Data centersCrew rooms near the site, phased with the build, removable when it is done.SchoolsFurnished rooms on district land, so a job offer comes with a place to live.Ski resortsPrivate rooms near the lifts, built over the summer, ready for seasonal hiring.Seasonal and islandsRooms for the busy season, raised on ground screws, removable when the need passes.Tribal nationsRooms for clinic, school and enterprise staff, and transitional housing.Defense and federalRooms beside the hub, the base or the yard, phased with the program.

THE UNITS

One shell family.
Built for crews and staff.

Every market on this page uses Outpost: private rooms with a factory-built bath pod and a kitchenette, on the same 4 ft wall module. Mix the layouts in one cluster.

Single or shared roomOne person, or two in twin beds, with one bath pod.Two private roomsTwo lockable rooms in one unit, each with its own bath pod.Accessible roomRoll-in bath pod and a steel ramp to the door.
